newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-FIVE OFF IN TWO MATCHES IN LIBERTADORES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIVE OFF IN TWO MATCHES IN LIBERTADORES.

text.p: Five players were sent off on a night of hot tempers in the South American Libertadores Cup on Tuesday.
Three players were shown the red card in the match between Gremio of Brazil and Peru's Sporting Cristal in first round, group four.
The tackles went flying in from the start, even though the match was of academic interest with both teams having already booked their places in the second round before the kick-off.
Striker Paulo Nunes, who scored Gremio's first goal in a 2-0 home win in Porto Alegre, was dismissed along with Norberto Solano and Manuel Marengo from the Peruvian champions.
Dauri scored the second goal as Gremio, the 1995 champions known for the physical style, finished atop of the group.
Cristal finished third, behind Brazil's Cruzeiro, but still went through as three of the four teams in the first round groups qualify. Alianza of Peru were eliminated.
Uruguay's Nacional finished with nine men against Deportivo Cali of Colombia after having Gustavo Badell and Aguiar shown the red card in the last five minutes in Montevideo.

The group five match ended 1-1, meaning that Cali must win their last match against Uruguayans Penarol on Friday to move ahead of Nacional into third place and join Penarol and Millonarios, of Colombia, in the next round.
Edson Mafla put Cali ahead with Julio Ravera equalising before halftime in a game dominated by the Colombians.
The other three first round groups have already been completed.
